projects.apexWorld.desc: Gamified CRM for NGO fundraising, built on a mix of complex systems: team and family hierarchies, duels, achievements, and leagues where every match changes with the event (team duels, everyone vs. a final boss, or royale rumble, a free-for-all). Each mode adds another layer of complexity.
projects.apexWorld.note: The project I work on actively as a hired developer.
projects.fort.desc: The mobile app version of Gymlogs: no API, mobile only.
projects.fort.note: Published on Google Play. Both the app and its landing page are open source.
projects.portfolio.desc: My current portfolio, the site you are on. I built it after the CMD one because I wanted something simpler that works on every device. I still like the CMD one, though.
projects.portfolioCmd.desc: An interactive CMD-style terminal portfolio with draggable windows and commands, in English and Spanish.
projects.portfolioCmd.note: Updated in 2026. Even I was surprised by some of the bad practices I committed back in 2024, when I started it.
projects.gymlogs.desc: A gym workout tracker, my end-of-degree final project, with a frontend and a backend. It is no longer online: Fort replaced it.
projects.gymlogs.note: Published in 2024. I kept the repository as a self-review: the code is annotated with the mistakes I made back then and what I would do differently today.
projects.chop.desc: A weekend project: a Go command-line tool to register different commands and run them on demand. It's called chop because in Spanish "chuleta" can mean either a meat chop or a cheatsheet.
projects.mediumFreeOnly.desc: A Chromium extension that hides the Medium stories that aren't free. Another weekend project, and my introduction to browser extensions.
projects.mediumFreeOnly.note: It detects premium stories with JS, hides them with CSS and requests more. It has performance issues; in the future it would be better to intercept Medium's API calls instead.
